edit.description: the seed gains the engine entry a case's spans start a shell through
the fixture proving the widened seed fires, beside the lane's own assertion
the span-rendering cases the widened scan reports declare the shared budget

summary: a default-lane case whose subject is inline-exec spans starts a shell per span, inherits vitest's 5s default, and the budget scan is blind to it

per.section: The default test lane must stay fast

acceptance: the spawn scan reports a default-lane case that renders inline-exec spans, and every site it reports declares the shared budget.
tests: the spawn scan reports a case that renders inline-exec spans without a declared budget
notes: Observed: tests/examples.test.ts's unreadable-artifact case timed out at vitest's 5s under full-suite contention, ~650ms alone. `sh` is no node launcher and the scan never follows an import, so NODE_COMMANDS cannot reach it — seed the render entry the spans go through, declared where NODE_COMMANDS is. The afterMerge gate runs this lane once per cherry-picked entry, so the flake reverts an innocent entry.

edit.description: the failing job's log sheds the forge's per-line framing before the tail trim
the shed, and the budget counting log lines, over the stub forge CLI

summary: a failing lane's log arrives with every line carrying the forge's job/step/timestamp prefix and ANSI codes, so the window's budget buys decoration instead of failing titles

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: the rendered lane block carries a failing job's log without the forge's per-line framing or ANSI codes, and the line budget is spent on log lines.
tests: a failing lane's log arrives without the forge's per-line job and step framing
a failing lane's log arrives without ANSI escape sequences
notes: Measured on the windows lane's 2026-09-15 run: ~1268 lines trimmed against the window's 1200-line budget, and 8 of the drained failures were keyable only by file:line because their titles sat in the trimmed head. Decoding the forge's own line framing is the package's GitHub-Actions opinion, beside `FORGE_CLI` — not a finding parsed out of the log. A lane-specific budget knob was the alternative; shedding needs no new surface.

edit.description: the inbox window's lane leg, beside the record and refusal legs
the reader reports the run's identity and whether it failed, for the leg to compare against the stamp
the slice stamps the run it drained, as it stamps a cursor
the lane leg over the stub forge CLI: red past the stamp, red already stamped, green, unreadable

summary: a declared lane never wakes the inbox slice, so a quiet tree hibernates over a red lane — and with no closing condition a woken lane would re-drain the same run every tick

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: the inbox slice is live for a declared lane exactly when that lane's latest completed run for the tip's branch failed and is past the lane's stamp; a green run, an already-stamped run, and a lane it cannot read each make it live for nothing.
tests: the inbox slice is live when a declared lane's latest completed run failed past the lane's stamp
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's failing run is the one already stamped
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's latest completed run passed
the inbox slice is not live when the forge CLI cannot read the lane
notes: `PlanSliceWindow.live` is sync and runs on the selection path (planState.ts), so the lane read has a sync half — once per tick per lane, beside the render's. `SliceInputs` carries no working tree, so the liveness leg must read the branch at the same repo root the render does (`ci.ts`, *The branch is the repo's*) or the two readers name different runs. The agent writes the stamp as it writes a cursor, so the rendered block must name the run it would stamp.

edit.description: the fixture root is canonicalized before anything composes a path from it
the runner fixture's own mkdtemp root, same treatment

summary: fixture roots come from `mkdtemp(tmpdir())` uncanonicalized, so every assertion comparing a composed path against git's worktree registry reads two spellings of one directory

per.section: A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote

acceptance: a fixture's repo root is the spelling git reports for it, and the registry assertions hold on a host whose temp dir is reached through a link.
tests: a fixture repo root is the path git reports for it, not the spelling the temp dir was named by
notes: 17 of the windows lane's 44 reds, in Dispatcher/worktrees/harnessRunner: expected `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` against git's `C:\Users\runneradmin\...`. The engine is not implicated — the reds are vacuity pins and registry-membership filters comparing the tester's spelling against the real writer's. Same class on macOS (`/var` -> `/private/var`), which is how the named test goes red on a POSIX base: drive the fixture with a temp root reached through a symlink.

edit.description: the silent arm takes absence from the path, not from an errno that means two things
the obstructed-root case, asserted on the refusal rather than on a platform's errno

summary: readAll reads `ENOENT` from the keyspace readdir as nothing-written, and on win32 a plain file at the prior-attempts root raises exactly that — an unreachable store reports as no records
acceptance: an obstructed prior-attempts root refuses on every supported host, and only a genuinely absent path reads as no records.
pins: readAll refuses when a plain file sits at the prior-attempts root
notes: Lane-observed: `readAll refuses when the prior-attempts dir is present but unreadable` resolved `Map{}` on windows-latest where POSIX raises ENOTDIR. The doc comment on readAll already names this exact degradation as the one it refuses to make. No `tests[]`: the errno split is unreproducible on a POSIX base, so the windows lane's own title is the verification (`spec/cli.md`, *win32 is a supported host*). Sibling ENOENT-means-absent arms in src/job.ts are not yet lane-evidenced.
